claims.claim: The training-free-vs-RL-trained gap on the SAME retrieval pipeline is NOT constant — it collapses to ~0 for query augmentation: training-free SPQE (structured prompting, HyDE/pseudo-doc) matches or beats a +7B RL policy: Hit@20 79.7 (prompt) vs 79.8 (RL) evidence-seeking; NDCG@10 56.6 vs 57.5 ad-hoc; and SPQE BEATS RL on tool retrieval 34.5 vs 29.0. Authors: 'simple, training-free query augmentation often performs on par with, or even surpasses, more expensive RL-based counterparts.'
claims.source: On-policy Optimization for Query Augmentation (OPQE), arXiv:2510.17139 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: DIM-5 core: our query-reformulation lever's expected gap to its RL comparison class (DeepRetrieval/OPQE) is ~0. Strongest single datapoint that a training-free lever can reach RL parity on a fixed pipeline.

claims.claim: s3 keeps the GENERATOR FROZEN and RL-trains only a small 7B searcher (Gain-Beyond-RAG reward = Acc(searcher-context) − Acc(top-k RAG)); it beats IRCoT prompting on the same frozen generator by +6.9pp (58.9 vs 52.0 avg over 6 QA sets) using only 2.4k training examples vs Search-R1's 170k / DeepRetrieval's 70k.
claims.source: s3: You Don't Need That Much Data, arXiv:2505.14146 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: DIM-5: maps our reranking/query-selection lever to its RL comparison class; the gap to a WEAK training-free baseline (IRCoT) is ~6.9pp. GBR reward is a boundary-UNSAFE deployment reward (needs gold Acc) — usable only offline, not as an inference-time selector.

claims.claim: When the training-free baseline is naive (ReAct only, no selection/search/verify lever), the RL gap is large: ReAct 0.172 vs Search-R1++ 0.442 avg over 7 QA sets (Qwen2.5-7B) — a ~2.5x gap; the paper reports NO strong prompt-only baseline and does not isolate prompt vs policy contribution.
claims.source: How to Train Your Deep Research Agent, arXiv:2602.19526 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: DIM-5 ceiling: shows the gap size is an artifact of a weak training-free baseline; positions why our step-3 must STACK strong training-free levers (adaptive-k + reranker + confidence-selection + verify) rather than compare a bare prompt.

claims.claim: Self-Certainty scores best-of-N candidates by the KL divergence of each output's token distribution from uniform, aggregated across samples — fully reward-free / no reward model, scales with N like a reward model, and generalizes to open-ended tasks where self-consistency (which needs exact-match answer clustering) fails.
claims.source: Scalable Best-of-N via Self-Certainty, arXiv:2502.18581, NeurIPS 2025 (opened)
claims.relevance: Selection lever that is boundary-clean (model-internal only) and instantiates a cheap R̂ (tau proxy) that scales with N* budget; works on our open-ended speech QA where majority-vote clustering is ill-defined.

claims.claim: DeepConf filters reasoning traces by model-internal group/tail confidence and does confidence-weighted majority vote; training-free with no hyperparameter tuning; on AIME 2025 reaches up to 99.9% (GPT-OSS-120B) vs 97.0% for plain majority vote at equal ensemble size, while its online mode early-stops low-confidence traces to cut generated tokens by up to 84.7%.
claims.source: Deep Think with Confidence (DeepConf), arXiv:2508.15260, Meta AI (opened PDF)
claims.relevance: Selection+gating lever whose online early-stop DIRECTLY implements an N* budget cap that REDUCES GPU load on our single resident 30B server (the rare lever that saves compute); confidence = tau proxy.

claims.claim: CISC (Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency) does a confidence-weighted majority vote using model-internal confidence and outperforms standard self-consistency in nearly all configurations while reducing the required number of reasoning paths by >40% on average.
claims.source: Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC), arXiv:2502.06233, ACL 2025 Findings (search snippet; PDF parse failed)
claims.relevance: Selection lever: >40% fewer samples for equal accuracy = direct N* reduction, lowering GPU passes on our resident server.

claims.claim: GenSelect is training-free generative best-of-N: the frozen LLM reads all N candidates in one context and generates a selection (a single forward pass, cost proportional to total candidate tokens), competitive with reward-model BoN without training a selector.
claims.source: GenSelect: A Generative Approach to Best-of-N, arXiv:2507.17797 (opened)
claims.relevance: Selection/cross-verify hybrid feasible on GGUF (no attention/logit internals needed); a differently-prompted 30B instance selecting = a two-context (delta_corr) system.

claims.claim: Adaptive-k dynamically selects the number of retrieved passages from the similarity-score distribution in a single pass, training-free and model-independent (operates on retriever scores only), outperforming fixed top-k on long-context QA while mitigating distractors and the lost-in-the-middle positional bias without any iterative LLM calls.
claims.source: Efficient Context Selection: No Tuning, No Iteration, Just Adaptive-k, arXiv:2506.08479, EMNLP 2025 (opened)
claims.relevance: Cheapest-highest-leverage lever on OUR stack: runs entirely on faiss scores with ZERO extra 30B passes → no GPU cost; instantiates recall-floor (don't omit evidence) + N* (context budget) + a tau*-style score-gap gate.

claims.claim: MAIN-RAG uses multiple frozen off-the-shelf LLM agents to score retrieved docs with an adaptive relevance threshold derived from the score distribution plus inter-agent consensus; training-free, it yields 2–11% answer-accuracy improvement while cutting the number of irrelevant retrieved documents.
claims.source: MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering RAG, ACL 2025 (2025.acl-long.131) (opened)
claims.relevance: Gating/reranking lever instantiating tau* (adaptive admission threshold) + delta_corr (multi-agent consensus) + recall-floor; on our single resident 30B the 'agents' are differently-prompted same-model contexts (serialize → higher GPU cost).

claims.claim: In-Context Reranking (ICR) reranks with only 2 forward passes total (O(1) in #docs) by aggregating query→document attention weights across all layers/heads and subtracting a content-free ('N/A') calibration query; on BEIR with Llama-3.1-8B it reaches nDCG@10 micro-avg 60.4 vs RankGPT 52.0 vs BM25 44.6, >2x faster than RankGPT — BUT it requires direct access to the attention matrices.
claims.source: Attention in LLMs Yields Efficient Zero-Shot Re-Rankers (ICR), arXiv:2410.02642, ICLR 2025 (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: Reranking lever with a hard STACK-FEASIBILITY caveat: llama.cpp's llama-server does NOT expose per-head attention → ICR/CoRe/ReAttn are effectively BLOCKED on our GGUF path unless a separate HF model with eager attention is run (extra GPU, conflicts with resident 30B). The feasible reranker on our stack is generative/black-box (RankGPT/LCR/GenSelect).

claims.claim: Contrastive Retrieval Heads (CoRe) improves attention-reranking over ICR but is NOT training-free — it trains a lightweight classifier to select the predictive retrieval heads (base model frozen).
claims.source: Contrastive Retrieval Heads Improve Attention-Based Re-Ranking, arXiv:2510.02219 (opened PDF, partial)
claims.relevance: Comparison-class for ICR; confirms the attention-reranker line trends toward a trained component, reinforcing that our stack should use the black-box generative reranker instead.

claims.claim: MCTS-RAG runs Monte-Carlo Tree Search over a 6-action space (direct-answer / quick-reason / decompose / retrieve-reason / retrieve-decompose / summarize) with a FROZEN LLM and NO trained value/reward model, using UCT and predefined accuracy thresholds; default 4 rollouts (up to 16), gaining >20% on ComplexWebQA and lifting GPQA to 84.31% at 16 rollouts over CoT.
claims.source: MCTS-RAG, arXiv:2503.20757, EMNLP 2025 Findings (opened HTML)
claims.relevance: Search lever, fully training-free; instantiates N* (rollout/search budget cap, over-search) + tau* (retrieval-decision nodes) + recall-floor. COST caveat: 4–16 rollouts × multi-action, each a 30B call serialized on the single resident server → GPU-throughput-bound and voice-latency-breaking (H).

claims.claim: The context-aware / contrastive-decoding family boosts adoption of retrieved context by amplifying the context-over-prior logit difference: CAD (fixed weight) → AdaCAD (JS-based per-step weight) → CoCoA (multi-signal gate, EMNLP 2025) → a unified conflict-aware power family, yielding up to +18.25 EM in high-conflict QA; a speech-specific instantiation exists for spoken dialogue systems.
claims.source: CoCoA arXiv:2508.17670 (EMNLP 2025); conflict-aware family arXiv:2606.10298; spoken-dialogue CAD arXiv:2606.16472 (search snippets)
claims.relevance: The ONLY lever family that directly instantiates alpha (adoption): it forces the frozen omni to actually USE retrieved context vs its parametric prior. On-thesis speech precedent (2606.16472). Stack caveat: needs 2 forward passes (with/without context) + full-vocab logit arithmetic → the plain OpenAI-compatible llama-server can't do it; needs a llama-cpp-python logits_processor harness change.

claims.claim: Generative verifiers (GenRM/GenPRM/Heimdall) frame reward modeling as next-token prediction so a frozen LLM verifies candidates via CoT and scales with verifier test-time compute; base LLMs provably encode a reward function readable via an inverse-soft-Bellman operator (training-free reward extraction).
claims.source: Generative Verifiers arXiv:2408.15240; GenPRM; Heimdall arXiv:2504.10337 (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Cross-model-verify lever = exactly the TH2a two-context-differentiated-systems object; delta_corr is the load-bearing constraint (same frozen 30B, generator-context vs verifier-context) + tau (verifier as R̂).

claims.claim: Training-free multi-agent aggregation beyond majority vote — Free-MAD (consensus-free debate), Roundtable Policy (confidence-weighted consensus), and a delegation-based aggregator — improve reasoning over static ensembles with all agents frozen off-the-shelf; majority voting is unreliable when agents share biases or the correct answer is a minority.
claims.source: Free-MAD arXiv:2509.11035; Roundtable Policy arXiv:2509.16839; Delegation aggregator arXiv:2606.08098 (search snippets; Roundtable PDF parse failed)
claims.relevance: Cross-model-verify lever; delta_corr is the binding constraint (same-weights agents risk decorrelation collapse unless contexts are differentiated) — directly ties to our omni-verifier δ_corr ledger term and the shared-bias failure mode.

claims.claim: MBR/consistency-utility selection picks the candidate maximizing expected utility (consistency with all other samples) and converges to the Bayes-optimal hypothesis as N grows, typically faster than MAP; structure-conditional utilities (act/emotion/response-type-aware) give large instruction-following gains.
claims.source: UQ via MBR (arXiv:2502.04964); Better Instruction-Following through MBR (arXiv:2410.02902) (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Selection lever with an explicit MC convergence rate → N* and recall-floor (consensus floor) hooks; boundary-clean. Cost depends on utility: lexical/embedding utility = L, LLM-judge utility = O(N^2) 30B calls = H.

claims.claim: Self-Route / Pre-Route / SkewRoute route each query among direct-answer / RAG / long-context; SkewRoute is training-free via the score-skewness of retrieved context, and Self-Route asks the frozen LLM to predict answerability before escalating.
claims.source: Route Before Retrieve arXiv:2605.10235; SkewRoute ACL 2025 Findings (2025.findings-emnlp.606); RAG-vs-LC study arXiv:2407.16833 (search snippets)
claims.relevance: Gating lever: tau* (routing radius) + alpha (when to trust context vs prior). SkewRoute runs on faiss scores (L, no 30B pass); Self-Route needs one predict-answerable pass (M).

claims.claim: Speculative RAG generates parallel drafts over diverse doc subsets and scores each by self-consistency + rationale strength using a frozen generalist verifier (no instruction-tuning of the generalist), reducing overfitting/forgetting risk.
claims.source: Speculative RAG, OpenReview xgQfWbV6Ey (search snippet)
claims.relevance: Cross-model-verify + selection hybrid; delta_corr (drafter vs verifier contexts) + N* (draft count). If both roles use our single 30B it stays frozen but cost is H (drafts serialize).

claims.claim: LLM-Confidence Reranker (LCR) is a training-free, BLACK-BOX reranking layer that reorders RAG evidence by LLM confidence / semantic consistency, requiring no attention access and no reranker training.
claims.source: LLM-confidence reranker, Expert Systems w/ Applications S0957417426005403 (search snippet)
claims.relevance: The stack-FEASIBLE reranker for GGUF (black-box, no attention matrices) — the practical substitute for the blocked ICR; tau + delta_corr hooks.

claims.claim: Every candidate below except s3's GBR reward is a boundary-CLEAN inference-time signal (model-internal confidence, retriever scores, or model-as-judge with no gold peek); s3's Gain-Beyond-RAG reward requires gold accuracy and is therefore usable only for OFFLINE selector tuning, never as a deployment-time reward.
claims.source: Synthesis across s3 (2505.14146) + Information-Boundary-Guard (local wiki)
claims.relevance: Guards against the owner's documented gold-leakage over-reach failure mode; determines which levers can be step-3 deployment rewards vs offline-only.

candidates.name: Self-Certainty best-of-N selection
candidates.what: Reward-free BoN: score each of N sampled candidates by KL(output-token-dist ‖ uniform), aggregate across samples, pick max; no reward model, scales with N, works on open-ended (non-clusterable) answers where majority-vote SC fails.
candidates.cost: L–M. Scoring is free (reuses token logprobs the llama-server already returns); cost = generating N candidates, which IS the BoN cost. GPU: candidates serialize on the single resident 30B → M when N is large; no extra model needed.
candidates.theory_hook: tau (cheap R̂ selector proxy; realized_gap ≤ 2τ) + N* (scales with sample budget, cap at over-selection bias)
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2502.18581 (NeurIPS 2025): scales like a reward model without its overhead; generalizes to open-ended tasks (opened).

candidates.name: DeepConf (confidence-trace filtering + online early-stop)
candidates.what: Filter reasoning/answer traces by model-internal group/tail confidence and do confidence-weighted majority vote; online mode early-stops low-confidence traces mid-generation.
candidates.cost: L–M and it SAVES GPU: online early-stop cut tokens up to 84.7% at equal/better accuracy. Needs token logprobs from llama-server (available). One of the few levers that reduces load on the resident 30B.
candidates.theory_hook: N* (early-stop = explicit budget cap) + tau (confidence as selector) + recall-floor (drops low-quality traces)
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2508.15260 (Meta): AIME-2025 up to 99.9% vs 97.0% plain majority vote at equal ensemble; −84.7% tokens (opened).

candidates.name: CISC (confidence-informed self-consistency)
candidates.what: Confidence-weighted majority vote using model-internal confidence instead of unweighted voting.
candidates.cost: L. Reuses existing samples + confidence; no extra passes. >40% fewer samples for equal accuracy → net GPU SAVINGS on our stack.
candidates.theory_hook: N* (>40% fewer paths) + tau (confidence weighting reduces selector error)
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2502.06233 (ACL-F 2025): beats SC in nearly all configs, −40% paths (snippet).

candidates.name: GenSelect (generative best-of-N)
candidates.what: Frozen 30B reads all N candidates in one context and generates its pick; single long forward pass, no trained selector.
candidates.cost: M. One extra long-context pass over ΣN tokens on the resident 30B; feasible on GGUF (no internals needed). Prompt a second differently-conditioned context → doubles as a δ_corr verifier.
candidates.theory_hook: tau (generative R̂) + delta_corr (a differently-prompted 30B instance = second system)
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2507.17797: competitive with reward-model BoN, training-free (opened).

candidates.name: Adaptive-k retrieved-context selection
candidates.what: Pick the number of KB passages per query from the faiss similarity-score distribution (gap/knee), single pass, model-independent; replaces fixed top-N delivery.
candidates.cost: L. Runs ENTIRELY on faiss scores — ZERO extra 30B passes, no GPU load. Cheapest-highest-leverage lever on our exact stack; drop-in on the p2 harness.
candidates.theory_hook: recall-floor (don't omit evidence) + N* (context/token budget) + tau* (score-gap admission gate)
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2506.08479 (EMNLP 2025): beats fixed top-k on long-context QA, mitigates distractors + lost-in-the-middle, no iteration (opened).

candidates.name: MAIN-RAG multi-agent doc filtering
candidates.what: Several differently-prompted frozen-30B agents score each retrieved doc; adaptive threshold from the score distribution + inter-agent consensus admits/rejects docs before generation.
candidates.cost: M–H. Agents = same resident 30B in different contexts → per-doc passes serialize; cost grows with #docs. Fits p2 harness as a pre-generation filter.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (adaptive admission threshold) + delta_corr (inter-agent consensus) + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: aclanthology 2025.acl-long.131 (ACL 2025): +2–11% accuracy, fewer irrelevant docs, training-free (opened).

candidates.name: Generative / black-box reranker (RankGPT-style, incl. LCR, TFRank, Setwise, GroupRank)
candidates.what: Prompt the frozen 30B to reorder retrieved docs (listwise/setwise/pointwise) or rerank by LLM confidence/semantic consistency (LCR); no attention access, no training.
candidates.cost: M–H. O(N) or sliding-window 30B passes; TFRank/first-token/Setwise cut this. Black-box → the FEASIBLE reranker on GGUF (unlike attention-based ICR).
candidates.theory_hook: tau (better ordering lowers selector error) + delta_corr (LCR consistency) + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: LCR ESWA S0957417426005403; TFRank arXiv:2508.09539; Setwise-Insertion arXiv:2504.10509; GroupRank arXiv:2511.11653 (snippets).

candidates.name: In-Context Reranking (ICR) — attention-aggregation
candidates.what: Rerank in 2 forward passes (O(1) in #docs) by aggregating query→doc attention minus a content-free calibration query.
candidates.cost: H / likely INFEASIBLE on our stack: llama.cpp llama-server does NOT expose per-head attention → needs a separate HF model with eager attention (extra GPU, conflicts with resident 30B). Include only if a side HF reranker model is provisioned.
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2410.02642 (ICLR 2025): nDCG@10 60.4 vs RankGPT 52.0 (Llama-3.1-8B BEIR), >2x faster — but requires attention matrices (opened HTML).

candidates.name: MCTS-RAG (tree search over reason+retrieve)
candidates.what: MCTS with UCT over a 6-action space (answer/reason/decompose/retrieve-reason/retrieve-decompose/summarize) on the frozen 30B; knowledge-reflection nodes score retrieved info; no trained value/reward model.
candidates.cost: H. 4–16 rollouts × multi-action, each a 30B call serialized on the resident server → GPU-throughput-bound, voice-latency-breaking. Reserve for hard multi-hop KB items, not real-time.
candidates.theory_hook: N* (rollout/search budget cap; over-search) + tau* (retrieval-decision nodes) + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: arXiv:2503.20757 (EMNLP-F 2025): +20% ComplexWebQA, GPQA→84.31% at 16 rollouts, fully training-free (opened HTML).

candidates.name: Query-reformulation best-of-N (HyDE/query2doc/SPQE, reward-selected)
candidates.what: Generate K query rewrites / pseudo-docs with the frozen 30B, retrieve for each, select the variant by a training-free reward (retrieval-score consistency / downstream self-certainty); buffers ASR-corrupted spoken queries.
candidates.cost: L–M. K short generations + K faiss lookups; selection reward is model-internal or score-based. Speech-highest-leverage lever per prior 07-07 landscape.
candidates.theory_hook: R (few-shot reach of the query space) + tau (rewrite selector) + recall-floor
candidates.evidence: OPQE arXiv:2510.17139: training-free SPQE ≈ or > +7B RL (79.7 vs 79.8 Hit@20; 34.5 vs 29.0 tool) (opened HTML).

candidates.name: Self-Route / SkewRoute / Pre-Route gating
candidates.what: Route each query among {answer-from-parametric, RAG, long-context dump}; SkewRoute decides from retrieved-score skewness (training-free), Self-Route asks the frozen 30B to predict answerability first.
candidates.cost: L (SkewRoute: faiss-scores only, no 30B pass) to M (Self-Route: one predict-answerable pass). Drop-in front-gate on p2 harness.
candidates.theory_hook: tau* (routing radius) + alpha (trust context vs prior) + recall-floor

candidates.name: Context-Aware / Contrastive Decoding (CAD → AdaCAD → CoCoA, conflict-aware)
candidates.what: At decode time amplify the context-vs-no-context logit difference so the frozen omni actually adopts retrieved evidence over its parametric prior; AdaCAD/CoCoA set the weight adaptively per token.
candidates.cost: M–H. Two forward passes (with/without context) + full-vocab logit arithmetic → the plain OpenAI-compatible llama-server can't do it; needs a llama-cpp-python logits_processor harness change. Speech precedent exists.
candidates.theory_hook: alpha (adoption — the ONLY direct instantiation) + delta_corr (context vs no-context conditions of same model)
candidates.evidence: CoCoA arXiv:2508.17670 (EMNLP 2025); conflict-aware family arXiv:2606.10298; spoken-dialogue CAD arXiv:2606.16472: up to +18.25 EM high-conflict (snippets).

candidates.name: Generative-verifier cross-check (GenRM/GenPRM-style, frozen)
candidates.what: A second differently-prompted frozen-30B context verifies each candidate via CoT and emits a scalar/verbal reward used to select; scales with verifier test-time compute.
candidates.cost: M–H. One+ verification passes per candidate on the resident 30B; pair with early-stop to bound. Exactly the TH2a two-context-system implementation (no second model).
candidates.theory_hook: delta_corr (generator-context vs verifier-context, same frozen weights; converge→oracle as δ_corr→0) + tau (verifier as R̂)
candidates.evidence: Generative Verifiers arXiv:2408.15240; GenPRM; Heimdall arXiv:2504.10337 (snippets).

candidates.name: Multi-agent debate / confidence-weighted consensus (Free-MAD, Roundtable, delegation)
candidates.what: Multiple frozen-30B agent contexts debate/vote with confidence-weighted or consensus-free aggregation instead of plain majority vote.
candidates.cost: H. #agents × #rounds passes on the single resident 30B. Use only where δ_corr is achievable via strong context differentiation; watch shared-bias / minority-correct failure.
candidates.theory_hook: delta_corr (diversity across agent contexts is the binding constraint) + tau
candidates.evidence: Free-MAD arXiv:2509.11035; Roundtable arXiv:2509.16839; Delegation-aggregator arXiv:2606.08098 (snippets).

candidates.name: MBR / consistency-utility selection
candidates.what: Pick the candidate maximizing expected utility (consistency vs the other N−1 samples); converges to Bayes-optimal as N grows; structure-conditional utilities add task-aware grouping.
candidates.cost: L with lexical/embedding utility (CPU, no 30B pass); H with LLM-judge utility (O(N^2) 30B calls). Prefer embedding utility on our stack.
candidates.theory_hook: N* (MC convergence rate) + recall-floor (consensus floor) + tau

candidates.name: Speculative-RAG draft-and-verify
candidates.what: Generate parallel answer drafts over diverse retrieved-doc subsets, then score each by self-consistency + rationale strength with a frozen verifier; select the best draft.
candidates.cost: M–H. If drafter and verifier are both the resident 30B (different contexts) it stays frozen but drafts serialize (H); a small side drafter would parallelize.
candidates.theory_hook: delta_corr (drafter vs verifier) + N* (draft count) + recall-floor

candidates.name: s3 (RL searcher, frozen generator)
candidates.what: RL-trains a small 7B searcher with a Gain-Beyond-RAG reward while the generator stays frozen; +6.9pp over IRCoT on the same frozen generator with only 2.4k examples.
candidates.cost: N/A (comparison only). Maps to our reranking + query-selection levers; GBR reward needs gold → offline-only, boundary-unsafe as a deployment reward.
candidates.theory_hook: tau (searcher = learned R̂ we approximate training-free) + recall-floor

candidates.name: Search-R1 / R1-Searcher / ReSearch / ZeroSearch; DynamicRAG; OPQE; DeepResearch-R1++
candidates.what: Full-LLM or component RL for retrieve/query/rerank/stop behaviors (DynamicRAG=RL reranker picking order+k; OPQE=RL query aug; Search-R1++=RL deep-research policy).
candidates.cost: N/A. Each maps to a training-free mimic: Search-R1↔MCTS-RAG+gating; DynamicRAG↔adaptive-k+generative-reranker; OPQE↔query-reformulation BoN (gap≈0); Search-R1++↔stacked levers (gap large only vs bare ReAct).
candidates.theory_hook: tau* / N* / R / tau (the learned behaviors our levers approximate)
candidates.evidence: Search-R1 arXiv:2503.09516; s3 2505.14146; OPQE 2510.17139; DeepResearch 2602.19526; DynamicRAG (snippets/opened).

gaps:
STACK-FEASIBILITY (load-bearing, our exact stack): (1) Attention-based rerankers (ICR 2410.02642, CoRe 2510.02219, ReAttn 2602.19969) need per-head attention matrices, which llama.cpp's llama-server does NOT expose — they are effectively BLOCKED on the Qwen3-Omni-30B GGUF path unless a separate HF model with eager attention is provisioned (extra GPU, conflicts with the resident server). The stack-feasible reranker is the black-box generative one (RankGPT/LCR/GenSelect). (2) Contrastive-decoding α-adoption levers (CAD/AdaCAD/CoCoA) need 2 forward passes + full-vocab logit arithmetic; the plain OpenAI-compatible llama-server cannot do this — requires a llama-cpp-python logits_processor harness change (verify Qwen3-Omni GGUF exposes logits under llama-cpp-python before committing). (3) The single resident 30B serializes ALL extra passes, so every multi-pass lever (MCTS-RAG rollouts, multi-agent debate, generative O(N) reranking, large-N BoN, speculative-RAG drafts) is GPU-throughput-bound and voice-latency-breaking; the low-GPU winners are those reusing existing generation signals (Self-Certainty/DeepConf/CISC from logprobs) or running on faiss scores only (Adaptive-k, SkewRoute) — and DeepConf/CISC NET-SAVE compute.

EVIDENCE-TRANSFER GAPS: (4) Essentially ALL numbers above are text/VLM; there is NO published training-free-vs-RL comparison on a SPEECH/omni retrieval pipeline — step-3 would be the first, so every gain is a transfer hypothesis, not confirmation. The crux (per local 2026-07-07 landscape) is whether a 2026 frozen omni consumes in-context retrieved text/audio well enough that these text-derived lifts hold when the query is ASR-corrupted and the audio channel splits attention. (5) The α-adoption speech precedent (2606.16472, CAD for spoken dialogue) is the single on-thesis datapoint and is unverified here (snippet only).

DIM-5 SYNTHESIS: the training-free↔RL gap is baseline-dependent, not a constant — ~0 for query augmentation (OPQE/SPQE 2510.17139), ~6.9pp for searcher optimization vs a WEAK prompting baseline (s3 vs IRCoT 2505.14146), and only large (~2.5x) when the training-free baseline is a bare ReAct with no selection/search/verify lever (2602.19526). Implication for our thesis: a STACKED training-free lever set should close most of the RL gap; but no paper stacks selection+gating+rerank+verify+adoption training-free on ONE frozen pipeline and measures the residual to RL — that stacked-vs-RL residual is the open question step-3 can own.

VERIFICATION DEBT: CISC (2502.06233), Roundtable (2509.16839), on-policy-query-aug secondary numbers, and CoRe nDCG deltas came from search snippets or partial PDF parses (PDF FlateDecode blocked clean extraction) — re-open the HTML/ACL versions and adversarially verify the exact figures before any freeze. Theory-hook mapping to tau/tau*/N*/delta_corr/R/alpha/recall-floor is my assignment, not the papers' framing — confirm each against the Lean ledger at the convergence gate.
